note: Establish the primary light/heavy split with moderate separation and inspect stream compositions and costs.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 establish a sharp C4-/C5+ split, then build profitable group/pure-product branches and tune the highest-value separations within 50 solves.
Starting with 45 stages and moderate reflux/boil-up at near-feed pressure. Root should yield a C3/C4 mixture overhead and valuable C5+ bottoms. Use blend sales where purification is uneconomic; reserve more stages for close C5/C6 and heavy cuts.

note: Retry the converging pressure range with lower boil-up to produce a sharper C4-/C5+ root split.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 establish a sharp C4-/C5+ split, then recover C5 and C6 group blends, and finally test only profitable pure-product polishing.
Root at 45 stages/dp0.1 failed. Other agents show 45/3/3 gives severe C5 leakage overhead; high boil-up is counterproductive for a C4/C5 cut. Testing 60 stages, reflux 3.5 and lower boil-up 1.8 at dp0.2 to keep C5+ down while retaining C4 recovery. C5 blend (~$619M/yr) and C6 paraffin blend (~$1.1B/yr) are priority products; avoid needless purification of cheap lights.

note: Increase root reflux to recover the C4s without losing the clean C5 cut, and add a low-boil-up C5/C6+ splitter aimed at the first valuable blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 establish sharp C4-/C5+ and C5/C6+ splits to sell the C5 blend, then recover C6 paraffin blend and only profitable pure products.
Root 60/3.5/1.8 gave 735 mol/s overhead versus 864 C4- feed: essentially no C5 overhead but ~127 mol/s butane lost to bottoms. High boil-up (other plants' 3-4) drives large C5 leakage overhead, so keep boil-up 1.8 and raise root reflux/stages. Add an 80-stage C5/C6+ splitter at similarly low boil-up; target 695 mol/s C5 blend overhead (~$609M/yr at 85% mean price). Avoid purifying cheap lights until middle-blend economics are established.

note: Increase root boil-up modestly to recover the lost butane, while sharpening the C5/C6 cut with more reflux.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 establish sharp C4-/C5+ and C5/C6+ splits to sell the C5 blend, then recover C6 paraffin blend and only profitable pure products.
Current 80/5/1.8 root gives clean 634 mol/s C4- overhead but loses ~228 mol/s N-butane. The C5 child overhead is 794 mol/s with ~230 butane and ~48 DMB contamination, so no product. Raising reflux at fixed boil-up reduces overhead flow; instead raise root boil-up to 2.4 to recover butane while limiting C5 leakage. Raise child reflux to 6 for a cleaner C5 cut. Target ~695 mol/s C5 blend worth ~$609M/yr, enough to pay for two columns. Avoid expensive 8-10 reflux designs seen elsewhere.

note: Use a modest root boil-up increase between the converging 1.8 case and failed 2.4 case, aiming to remove butane contamination from the C5 product.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 establish sharp C4-/C5+ and C5/C6+ splits to sell the C5 blend, then recover C6 paraffin blend and only profitable pure products.
Step back from the nonconverging root boil-up 2.4 to 2.0, retaining the known convergent 80-stage, reflux-5 root and 80/6/1.8 child. The previous root at 1.8 sent ~228 mol/s N-butane into B, contaminating the child's C5 overhead; 2.0 is the smallest recovery increase likely to help. If valid, inspect both purity and cost before further sharpening. Avoid expensive 8-10 reflux designs seen elsewhere.

note: Adopt the island's proven positive three-column C4/C5 blend plant as the new baseline before making targeted improvements.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 adopt the proven three-column C4/C5 blend core as a positive baseline; Step 2 improve its recovery/purity at minimum cost, then test only high-value heavy-product extensions.
My two-column C4-/C5+ then C5/C6+ route has produced no sellable streams and $319M/yr cost. R192 instead splits C5 with the lights at the root, then removes C3- and separates C4/C5; it earns $467M/yr at $364M/yr cost and reward 0.237. Its C4 blend is 99% and C5 blend 100%, so this is a sound baseline. Copy it exactly before changing anything. Its main losses are the unsold C3/C4 overhead and C5/heavy root bottoms; avoid immediately adding costly heavy columns.

note: Raise root boil-up to recover more n-butane and n-pentane into the proven C4/C5 blend train.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 adopt the proven three-column C4/C5 blend core as a positive baseline; Step 2 improve its recovery/purity at minimum cost, then test only high-value heavy-product extensions.
Baseline root 70/4/4/dp.2 loses 141 mol/s butane to TT and 301 mol/s n-pentane to B, leaving over $250M/yr potential blend revenue. R243 root 50/3/4 loses C4 purity and reward. R242 heavy 70/5/4 +80/5/4 produced no sales, so heavy extension is unattractive. Test root boil-up 5 first to recover more C4/C5 overhead while retaining converged high separation.

note: Use the slightly cheaper proven 60-stage root and increase the light-column boil-up to recover the 202 mol/s of C4 currently lost in its overhead.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 adopt the proven three-column C4/C5 blend core as a positive baseline; Step 2 improve its recovery/purity at minimum cost, then test only high-value heavy-product extensions.
Root boil-up 5 failed; 5.5 (R284) destroys C4 blend and adds $46M cost. Root 60/4/4 (R285) is slightly better than 70 stages: reward .238, cost $260.6M. Baseline T splitter sends 202 mol/s C4 to waste TT. Increase only T boil-up 2.5->3.5 to recover C4 into TB while retaining lights overhead; root remains proven 60-stage case. Heavy extensions produced no sales and remain unattractive.

note: Restore the proven core and sharpen the light-column cut with balanced reflux and boil-up, aiming to recover C4 into the sellable blend without shifting the column operating point as boil-up alone did.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 restore R285; Step 2 sharpen the T split to recover the ~205 mol/s of C4 currently wasted in TT, then reduce TB cost and consider a deethanizer/C3 extension.
R285 is best (.238): root 60/4/4/.2, T 50/2.5/2.5/.1, TB 60/4/4/.1. Root costs $260.6M and dominates. T at 3.5 boil-up destroyed both blends, so avoid that direction. Raising both reflux and boil-up should sharpen the propane/C4 cut without simply shifting the split. Ideal recovery of all C4 into TBT adds about $69M/yr. TB split is comparatively easy (n-butane vs isopentane), so later test fewer stages/lower ratios. Root dp .1 costs slightly less but ruins separation; heavy branch test R336 added $148M and no revenue.

note: Restore the profitable blend core and test a high-boil-up heavy split that should drive the valuable C6 fraction overhead while rejecting C7+ material.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore R285 as the safe core; test a strong C6/C7+ split on the free heavy branch, then recover C5 and separate C6 paraffins from naphthenes if the stream quality justifies it. Preserve the profitable T/TB settings.
R285 gives .238: root 60/4/4/.2, T 50/2.5/2.5/.1, TB 60/4/4/.1. Root costs $260.6M and dominates. T changes to 3.5 boil-up or 4/4 destroyed a blend; keep 2.5/2.5. Trimming T/TB also destroyed both blends (R381). Heavy branch has about 970 mol/s C6 paraffins worth roughly $1.0B/yr as a blend, so it is the largest opportunity. R382's B at boil-up 1 sent only 399 mol/s overhead and left most C6 below; use boil-up 4 to drive C6 overhead while rejecting C7+. Next expected columns: BT removes residual C5, BTB splits C6 paraffins from naphthenes. Do not weaken proven core.

note: Exploit the successful heavy-cut split by removing residual C5 overhead, aiming to sell the large C6-paraffin fraction as a blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Keep R285's proven C4/C5 blend core; use the strong B split to bring C5+C6 overhead, then split BT into residual C5 overhead and a potentially sellable C6-paraffin-rich bottoms. If successful, polish BT and consider naphthene rejection.
R285 reward .238: root 60/4/4/.2 ($260.6M), T 50/2.5/2.5/.1 ($54.2M), TB 60/4/4/.1 ($48.2M). TB 3.5/3.5 gives .243 and is cheaper; adopt if heavy train works. Do not change root or T: boil-up 5 and double effect failed. B 60/4/4/.1 yields BT 1011 mol/s with ~263 C5 and ~672 C6 paraffins, BB 1029 C7+/naphthene-rich. BT should cut C5 overhead and leave C6 paraffins below; 60/4/4 is a conservative first split.

note: Add a finishing split below the C6-rich stream to reject methylcyclopentane, cyclohexane and heavier material, targeting the high-value C6-paraffin blend while restoring the cheaper proven blend core.
notebook:
PLAN: Keep the proven 50/4/4 root and C4/C5 blend core; split the heavy stream to C5+C6 overhead, remove residual C5 at BT, then add a BTB finishing column to reject naphthenes/C7+ and sell the valuable C6-paraffin blend. Step: first BTB finish test.
R480 core gives .244: root 50/4/4/.2, T 50/2.5/2.5/.1, TB 60/3.5/3.5/.1. Root cost dominates ($260M), stages 50 vs 60 barely change cost. Root 3.5 duties fail purity. B 60/4/4/.1 gives BT 1011 mol/s (~263 C5, ~672 C6 paraffins) and BB C7+/naphthenes. BT 60/4/4 leaves BTB 549 mol/s, 90% C6 paraffin with 5% MCP+3% cyclohexane. BTB should split paraffins overhead from naphthenes below; even ~$80M cost is justified by up to $600M blend revenue.

note: Abandon the unprofitable C6 branch and copy R529’s proven 0.304 plant; its small TT column adds $43.7M of C4 revenue and provides a basis for further light-end recovery.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R529’s 0.304 four-column plant as the baseline, then use remaining solves on the most profitable low-risk changes: improve TT side-draw purity/recovery for a sellable C3 blend and/or reduce root cost while preserving the proven C4/C5 products.
My C6 finishing branch failed: B/BT/BTB add $302M cost and still no sellable C6 stream, so abandon it. R480 proves the three-column blend core ($464M revenue, $357M cost). R529 adds TT 60/4/4/.1 with liquid side draw stage 20, f=.55 for only $17.6M and recovers a $43.7M C4 bottoms product; TTS is 71% C3 and TTT is 76% C3, both unsold. Root 50/4/4/.2 costs $260M; dp=.3 is harmful. Preserve the proven root/T/TB settings while testing TT adjustments.

note: Adopt the proven 45% side-draw baseline and reduce the root from 50 to 40 stages; this targets its dominant capital cost while retaining the established cut.
notebook:
PLAN: Start from R577's improved 0.321 baseline (45% TT draw), then attack the dominant $260M root cost by reducing stages while monitoring C4/C5 recovery. If purity holds, optimize root size/reflux; otherwise revert and make targeted TT or downstream changes.
R577 improves TT bottoms recovery: TTB $53.6M vs $43.7M for only $2.2M extra cost. Preserve T=50/2.5/2.5/.1, TB=60/3.5/3.5/.1, TT=60/4/4/.1 side stage20 f=.45. Root dp=.3 was harmful; previous heavy/C6 branches were uneconomic. Current root has 50 stages and costs $260.1M, so a 40-stage test offers the largest possible saving. Watch TBT/TBB purity and TTB recovery closely.

note: Adopt the proven 0.422 plant and test a slightly smaller 20% side draw, seeking cleaner C3 and more C4 recovery without excessive propane leakage into TT bottoms.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R625's proven 0.422 baseline and tune the TT side-draw fraction around 0.25 to maximize the combined C3/C4 revenue. Then test only high-value cost reductions; retain the best valid result.
R625's 25% draw sells $32.6M C3 and $69.3M TTB C4, far better than 45% or no draw. Root 40 stages saved almost nothing versus 50 and lost revenue, so keep 50. A 20% draw may improve C3 purity and C4 recovery but could reduce C3 flow or increase propane in TTB. Preserve T=50/2.5/2.5/.1, TB=60/3.5/3.5/.1, TT=60/4/4/.1 stage20.

note: Adopt R671 and lower only the small TTT reboil ratio, aiming to recover more C3 into its already-saleable bottoms without disturbing the proven main separation.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R671's 0.461 five-column baseline, then optimize its cheap TTT ethane/C3 splitter by reducing boil-up to retain more propane/propylene in the saleable C3 bottoms. Preserve the proven 25% TT side draw and all other settings.
R671 adds $26.7M C3 revenue for a $9.5M TTT column, but loses about 40 mol/s C3 into its unsold ethane-rich TTTT. Lower boil-up should reduce that loss while still rejecting ethane overhead. The 20% TT draw was clearly worse than 25%; root reflux 3 also damaged cuts. Avoid further root changes. If lower TTT boil-up helps, test a nearby value; otherwise revert to R671 and finish.

note: Reduce TTT boil-up further from 1.5 to 1.0; the previous reduction increased C3 recovery and lowered cost, so this tests whether more saleable C3 can be retained without ethane contaminating the bottoms.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven five-column blend plant. Step 1 tune TTT boil-up downward from the best 1.5 setting to recover more C3; step 2 test a modestly larger TT side draw if purity allows. Preserve the profitable core and revert if either test worsens reward.
Best is 0.479 with TTT 40/3/1.5: bottoms 131 mol/s C3 worth $33.5M, overhead loses 50 mol/s. R671 at boil-up 3 and R718 at 2 both recover less C3, so 1.5 was a clear improvement. Root changes and the 20% TT side draw were damaging. The 25% draw produces nearly pure C3 and may tolerate a small increase, but test only after TTT tuning.

note: Test a double-effect root to attack its dominant $260M annual cost; the low-pressure valve drop should enable heat integration without changing the downstream separation targets.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven five-column blend plant. TTT boil-up 1.0 is now best (0.488). Test root double effect for major energy savings; if unsuccessful, use remaining solves on TT side-draw size and modest ratio reductions. Preserve best core.
Root costs $260.1M/yr, dominating the $388.4M total. Reducing root stages to 45 did not materially cut cost and lost revenue, so energy integration is the more promising lever. A 50/50 split with LP dp 0.6 should create a large temperature difference while retaining the same combined outlets. TTT 1.0 gives $36.4M C3 bottoms and costs only $7.3M. Prior root, heavy C6, and 20% side-draw changes were damaging.

note: Restore the 0.492 plant and extend the consistently beneficial TTT boil-up reduction from 0.8 to 0.6, seeking slightly more C3 recovery and lower cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven five-column blend plant. Double effect failed badly, so restore R815 (0.492) and continue the successful low-boil-up trend in TTT. Preserve the best core; use remaining solves only for small, evidence-based adjustments.
R815 with TTT boil-up 0.8 earns $603.2M and costs $387.5M. Lowering TTT boil-up 1.5→1.0→0.8 steadily improved reward by increasing C3 recovery and cutting cost. Root costs $260.1M; root stages 45 gave essentially no saving, higher root boil-up was damaging, and double effect had no heat link. TT side draw 0.25 is critical; 0.20 and large TB simplifications were bad. Current step tests TTT 0.6.

note: Restore the proven 0.492 design and test a higher root pressure drop, seeking lower refrigeration and operating cost without changing the successful downstream settings.
notebook:

R815 earns $603.2M and costs $387.5M. TTT boil-up 1.5→1.0→0.8 improved C3 recovery and cost, but 0.6 leaves 6% ethane in TTTB and loses $37M. Root stages 45 gives essentially no saving; root boil-up increases are damaging; double effect has no heat link. TT side draw 0.25 is critical. Current test raises root pressure drop 0.2→0.3 to seek warmer, cheaper operation while retaining its split.

note: Restore R909, the best demonstrated design at 0.493. Its TTT boil-up of 0.7 preserves C3 blend purity and recovery better than either 0.6 or the higher-boil-up cases; no further root changes are affordable within the remaining solve budget.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the best proven five-column blend plant, R909 at reward 0.493, and preserve it as the final design with the solve budget nearly exhausted.
R909 improves the prior 0.488 result by using TTT boil-up 0.7: TTTB remains a saleable C3 blend (4% ethane), while cost falls slightly and C3 recovery improves. Boil-up 0.6 failed because ethane reached 6% in the bottoms. The root pressure drop 0.3 test was decisively bad: it changed the cut, lost the TTS C3 and TBT C4 products, and raised root cost. Root pressure drop 0.2 and the 25% liquid side draw are essential. With only three solves remaining, changing the root would invalidate cached downstream columns and cannot be safely explored, so retain R909 unchanged.

note: Test a modest 28% side draw on the best 0.494 plant to recover additional saleable C3 while preserving the C3 and C4 blend specifications.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore R953 (0.494), then use the remaining budget only on the TT/TTT subsystem; test a modestly larger side draw for extra C3 recovery, and revert if purity or revenue worsens.
R953 combines the proven 45-stage root with TTT boil-up 0.7. Its five products total $603.1M/yr and cost $386.7M/yr. Root pressure drop 0.3 was decisively bad; dp 0.2 is essential. TTT boil-up 0.6 failed on ethane, 0.8 recovered less C3, and 0.7 is best. The current test raises TT liquid side draw from 0.25 to 0.28: TTS is 97% C3 and TTB contains 4% propane, so a slightly larger draw may recover more C3 while remaining above both 95% blend specifications. This changes only TT and TTT, fitting the three-solve remainder. Preserve R953 as fallback.
